$comment: The cross-language mirror inventory (docs/FRONTEND.md, Cross-language mirrors).
Every mirror that survives #236's payload contract and #239's module extraction is
listed here with the proof that holds it. `tests/test_mirrors.py` derives candidate
mirrors from the tree with `tests/cross_language_mirrors.py` and holds this file to
the result in both directions, so an undeclared mirror and a stale declaration each
fail `make check`.
`evidence` is what the derivation found, and is the drift detector for a mirror
whose whole content is a shared string: change the words on either side and the
declared evidence stops being derived. It is empty for a mirror the derivation
cannot see -- arithmetic and structure share no words -- which is why those carry a
generated fixture instead.
`proof` values:
parity-fixture       cases in tests/js/fixtures/mirror-parity.json, generated by
tests/mirror_parity.py and asserted by
tests/js/mirror-parity.test.mjs.
lens-parity-fixture  cases in tests/js/fixtures/lens-parity.json.
markup-parity        the audited-page region diff in tests/js/*-markup-parity.test.mjs
renders the lit half and compares it with the Jinja half.
shared-literal       the mirror is one constant string; the derived text evidence
is itself the check, because changing either side removes it.
payload-carried      the rule's preferred outcome: the server publishes the value
and the client reads it rather than recomputing it.

share-percentage-label.note: A whole percentage over exact integer arithmetic on both sides. Shares no words with its server half, so only the fixture can see it drift; the fixture's boundary shares are the exact halves a float round would land on the wrong side of. `meter_candidate_percentage` (#325) names this function's own half-up rounding rule in its docstring as the precedent it follows for a section meter's own percent, which is what the symbol evidence now catches — it is a citation of the rule, not a second call site, so it earns no new fixture case here.

endorsement-count-label.note: Meter v2's caption tally ('21½ of 23 endorsements', docs/METER_V2.md § Counting): an exact rational as a mixed number with vulgar-fraction glyphs, never a float — the mockup's float formatter is illustrative only. A fractional part outside the glyph set falls back to numerator⁄denominator with the fraction slash. Landed ahead of the surfaces (#312), so nothing renders it yet; the fixture is what holds the two sides together until a caption does.

meter-layout-blocks.note: Meter v2's whole layout (docs/METER_V2.md § Splits: placement and the tongue rule): cells in, an ordered block list out, which both renderers consume verbatim. The two sides receive the same cells in different orders — the server iterates race.source_cells in active-source order, the lens payload delivers sorted transport codes — so the ordering rules are the mirror, and they share no display text at all. The fixture's published cases come from the races page_parity.py's feature census already selects; a three-way split and two adjacent split bands are hand-built, because this election's ballot contains neither. #314 gave the layout's admission rule — which cell states draw a block, and the explicit exclusion of a declining source's denominator weight — one production home, `meter_endorsements`, which this fixture's cases are built from too (closing a deferred finding from #313's review: the rule used to live only in the fixture generator).

no-majority.note: At or below half, not merely behind the leader. The threshold is a comparison rather than a string, so the shared qualifier text alone would not catch a flipped inequality.

meter-standings.note: The meter's own rank order — leader first, ties broken by display label then id — which its color assignment and accessible name both read (docs/METER_V2.md § Color; Splits: the tongue rule). `meter_units` and `meter_candidate_labels` are the two small helpers it and every downstream meter mirror share; none has display text of its own, so the derivation finds them only by the doc comments naming them, and this entry is where those comments point.

meter-accessible-label.note: The meter's spoken name under meter v2 (docs/METER_V2.md, The discovery model's accessibility model): the full standings, not the resting percentage — replacing screen_share_accessible_label/shareAccessibleLabel, which this ticket deleted (see `deleted` below). Empty standings is the N/A state's own name, the one piece of literal text the derivation can see; the standings sentence itself is built from `endorsement_count_label` output, which shares no further words across languages.

meter-candidate-colors.note: Each standing candidate's block color (docs/METER_V2.md § Color): the site's own teal or amber for a sole leader, the tie/trailing pools by rank otherwise, stepping toward the track once a pool runs out (Decision log #18). Color-pool exhaustion is not reachable by this election's data — no race runs four trailing candidates or three tied leaders deep — so the fixture's exhaustion cases are hand-built standings, the same reason meter-layout-blocks hand-builds shapes the ballot cannot reach.

meter-block-renders.note: Every block's complete paint (the inline `style` value MeterBlockRender carries, built once so a Jinja macro and a lit-html template both merely write it rather than assembling it twice) and tooltip decision text (docs/METER_V2.md, The discovery model). `meter_block_decision`'s own text — 'Endorsed', the split phrasing, the two-way glyph and the literal n-way ratio — is folded in here rather than given its own entry, because every case that reaches a decision branch reaches it by rendering blocks. A seam is two half colors (top, bottom), not one — a boundary between two different splits in one band shares its top half's color but not its bottom half's, which a single shared seam color painted wrong until this function paired the halves; `--{prefix}-color`/`--{prefix}-image` (a flat, transitionable color when both halves agree, a two-stop border-image gradient when they do not) is what the derivation's `--•-color:`/`--•-image:...` entries name. That two-split-band case, the n-way share, and the color-mix seam blends are only reachable through meter-layout-blocks' hand-built shapes (a three-way split, adjacent bands), which this fixture reuses for the same reason that entry does.

meter-candidate-block-contexts.note: One candidate's bold/recede class-name suffixes for every block of the shared, once-per-race layout (docs/METER_V2.md, Color; #325): the race-detail page's per-candidate section meter reads these alongside meter-block-renders' own style, never re-deriving which blocks name a candidate. Shares no display text with its server half — the values are CSS class-name fragments, not words a reader sees — so only the fixture, exercised against meter-layout-blocks' own hand-built shapes (a three-way split, adjacent bands, a non-adjacent split), can see the two sides disagree about which half bolds and which recedes.

meter-candidate-accessible-label.note: One candidate's own section meter's spoken name (docs/METER_V2.md, The discovery model's accessibility model, extended to the per-candidate meter in #325): '<name>: 21½ of 23 endorsements', this candidate's own exact count against the race's whole denominator — not the full-standings sentence meter-accessible-label states for the (now retired) shared headline bar. The colon-led template is the one piece of literal text the derivation can see; the count itself is built from endorsement_count_label output, which shares no further words across languages.

meter-candidate-percentage.note: One candidate's own resting percent (docs/METER_V2.md, Resting label; #325's own decision log), rounded half-up on exact rational arithmetic — the same whole-percent rounding rule share-percentage-label already proves at the race's own leader-share boundaries, applied here to any standing candidate's own denominator instead of only the race's overall winner share. A bare number, not a labeled string, so it shares no words with its server half; only the fixture's boundary shares can see the two sides round one differently.

meter-markup.note: The meter's own markup shape — the container's class list and the block class list — held together by guide-markup-parity.test.mjs and race-markup-parity.test.mjs, which diff the audited page's [data-lens-result] region against the lit render node for node. Both renderers read one precomputed MeterView/MeterBlockRender rather than deciding a class list twice; this entry is what a Jinja macro naming a lit template by name puts in the inventory. `meterBlockTemplate` became a second, directly named export in #325, when the race-detail page's per-candidate section meter (`candidate_meter` in `_meter.html.j2`) started reusing the exact same block markup rather than a second implementation — held by the same region diff, since a candidate section is inside `[data-race-candidates]`, the fourth region `race-markup-parity.test.mjs` already covers.

support-summary.note: The meter's own caption (I39), redesigned in #314 to state the recommended choice's exact endorsement count rather than only the denominator (docs/METER_V2.md, Caption): '21½ of 23 endorsements'. Revised in #314's own review to drop the recommended choice's name from the sentence entirely — every card that renders this caption already carries that name one row up, in the headline, so the name here was pure restatement. A tie or a race with no single recommended choice falls back to the caption's pre-v2 wording, which is the branch the shared text evidence catches. Mirrored only in the no-lens branch; with a selection the client states a count against the selected total instead (H38), which the server has no wording for.

support-summary-compact.note: The compact caption's own redesign: the leader's count, with the name dropped too — the card's own heading already carries it. Falls back to the bare denominator ('N sources') for the same no-single-leader reason support-summary does.

recommendation-label.server: publication/builder.py recommendation_label, held by models.py validate_display_semantics
recommendation-label.note: Sole leader, tie, and insufficiency each choose different words. The fixture's panels reach all three from real bundles.

race-detail-support-summary.note: The client names its counterpart in a comment. That claim is what put this entry here; the fixture is what makes it true.

race-detail-accessible-summary.note: The mirror #240 was opened for. The audited value is carried in the payload since #236; this recomputes it while a lens is active, which is why the function survives.

counting-summary.server: guide.html.j2 lens banner and sources.html.j2 page count
counting-summary.note: Template text rather than a function, so the fixture reads its expectation out of the committed audited pages.

tallying-source-count.note: The number inside the counting sentence, and its own mirror: the guide counts contributing consensus sources in Jinja while the client counts non-comparison payload sources. Two predicates over two collections that have to reach one total, or the banner changes the instant a reader touches the page.

comparison-percentage-label.note: The one FRONTEND.md recorded as owed. Markup parity reaches only the baseline column's share; a category column's share is computed on the client and rendered nowhere on the audited page, so the boundary cases are the only way to see it.

comparison-row-differs.note: Set logic over lead sets, sharing no text at all. Neutral cells are the interesting half: a blank column must neither agree nor create a difference.

compare-fragment-encoding.note: The encoding mirror, which § Cross-language mirrors names as a category and which is the only one left. Python composes the preset fragments the Comparisons page renders as links; the client composes the same fragment for every state change after that. Both spell the same parameter names in the same canonical order, the same cmp=1 schema version, and the same twelve-character panel-hash prefix — panel_hash[:12] against HASH_PREFIX_LENGTH = 12. It shares no display text and neither side names the other, so no derivation signal can see it: this entry exists because a reviewer put it there, which is the floor-not-ceiling rule doing its work. Drift here is quiet rather than loud — a preset link decodes as stale_version and the page loads on its default columns instead of the ones the link asked for.
compare-fragment-encoding.known_asymmetry: The two sides agree on every column set the server produces, but not on which sets are legal. compare-url.mjs guards encodeCompareFragment with MIN_COLUMNS = 2 and MAX_COLUMNS = 3; comparison_fragment has no matching guard. Every preset in rendering/documents.py asks for two columns, so nothing is wrong today, but a one- or four-column preset would render a link the client refuses to decode. The golden cases stay inside the range both sides admit rather than asserting a shape only one of them has an opinion about.

lens-scoring.note: The pattern every other entry follows. Its fixture predates this inventory and is generated by publication/lens_parity.py.

meter-unavailable-label.server: guide.html.j2 empty meter, asserted by rendering/validation.py _html_semantic_values
meter-unavailable-label.note: The meter's visible text for a race with no share, and the sibling of the divergence this ticket found one line away: the spoken label says 'not available' while both sides show 'N/A'. The server writes the literal in the template rather than in a function, but validation.py already spells the whole rule as an expression — 'N/A' if percentage_whole is None else percentage_label — so that is the oracle for both branches. The audited dataset renders no null-share race, so markup parity cannot reach this any more than it could reach the spoken half.

no-majority-pill.note: A third spelling of the qualifier, after 'No majority.' in the accessible summaries and 'No majority ·' in the dialog kicker. This one is inside a card region guide-markup-parity diffs against the audited page, so the rendered markup is what holds it.

comparison-differs-badge.note: The badge marking a race whose columns disagree. Written inside a conditional lit sub-template, which is the shape that hid it: a nested `html` template inside a `${...}` inside a template literal. The audited page renders twelve of these inside the row groups compare-markup-parity diffs, so the pair is held there; the entry exists so it is also named.

sources-also-in-tag.note: The tags themselves are payload-carried (#248); the two words introducing them are not, and sources-markup-parity diffs the region that renders them.

blank-comparison-cell-dash.note: The em dash a cell shows when a source published no endorsement. Inside the row groups compare-markup-parity diffs. Its `title` explanation is an attribute, which neither side's scan reads — the markup diff does compare attributes, so the pair is still held.

view-toggle-labels.note: The filter status line names the current view using the same two words the toggle is labelled with, so a reader hears the label they just pressed. The server renders the control, the client composes the announcement, and neither reads the other's text.

comparison-race-heading.note: The other heading in the same row as all-sources-column-label, and unguarded for the same reason: the comparison head is deliberately outside the markup-parity claim. One word, so the derivation is the whole check — and it took widening the scan past its space-requiring filter to see it at all.

default-comparison-columns.note: Category codes, not display text — the scan reaches them because a capitalized token is not syntax. The payload publishes every category with its code and label, and the client resolves labels through it; these literals are a preference order for which columns to offer first, which the server does not compute. Nothing is spelled twice except the codes themselves, and tests/test_client_payload_types.py holds the client to the published catalog.

grade-vocabulary.server: scoring/models.py Grade, via the payload generator
grade-vocabulary.note: The grade strings have one generator, as § Shared names requires: the client's ComputedGrade is generated from the audited engine's Grade, and tests/test_client_payload_types.py fails when the two vocabularies stop matching. The client compares against these strings rather than redefining them.

audited-candidate-order.note: The order a race page puts its candidate sections back into when a lens clears. It is the payload's own race.candidates, published from the order the renderer rendered, because the two sides break a tie differently: the renderer orders equal support by display label and the client's standings order it by ballot position. Recomputing put a tie's two candidates back in the wrong order, which is what race-markup-parity.test.mjs caught -- so the client names the server's function only to record that it does not reimplement it. The deleted map below carries the same removal for the guide, from #236.

race-detail-lens-kicker.note: One word a race page shows above a tied candidate, written as a Jinja branch on one side and a ternary on the other. 'Leading choice' left this mirror when the headline became the sole leader's own heading: the server spells it there and the client only shows or hides that block, so it is no longer written twice. 'No majority ·' went with it — the qualifier is the headline's pill now, and the accessible summaries spell their own 'No majority.', which is mirrored under its own key.

comparison-control-status.server: compare.html.j2, the status argument to election_controls
comparison-control-status.note: The Comparisons control bar's status line. The server composes it in a Jinja concatenation passed as a macro argument; the client assigns its own with textContent, outside the lit regions compare-markup-parity diffs. Both sentences reduce to one template, so a word or a placeholder moving on either side alone stops the evidence being derived.

all-sources-column-label.note: The comparison head is deliberately outside the markup-parity claim, because the audited page cannot render column controls that do nothing without JavaScript. What is left to agree on is two words, and the derivation sees them.

outside-scope-cell-text.note: Also inside the region compare-markup-parity diffs, but only for a race the audited data puts a source outside. The literal is checked whether or not that race exists.

audited-insufficient-note.server: guide.html.j2 race card, asserted by rendering/validation.py
evidence: text:Too few endorsements to measure agreement.
audited-insufficient-note.note: The audited dataset grades no race insufficient, so no markup diff can render this note. Its words are the whole mirror, so the derivation is the check.

election-day-external-link-attributes.client: election-day.mjs EXTERNAL_LINK_ATTRIBUTES, the counting state's King County Elections link
election-day-external-link-attributes.note: #285's counting state is the one link election-day.mjs ever writes itself, so it restates the site's one external-link convention rather than importing it -- these are hand-written ES modules with no bundler (election-day.mjs's own module comment). The symbol reference is a comment, not a second implementation: election_day_banner_html renders the certified state directly and drops data-election-day entirely once results exist, so wireElectionDay's querySelector finds nothing and the two states never run the same code. 'election-day phrasing' (deleted, above) still holds for the dates themselves -- shell.py formats every date the counting state shows; the client chooses copy and links, never a date.

race-results-counting-text.client: election-day.mjs, the banner's own counting-state sentence
race-results-counting-text.server: guide.html.j2, a candidate race card's own counting note
race-results-counting-text.note: #286 deliberately reuses the banner's own counting-state wording (docs/RESULTS.md, Rendering § Race cards: 'per #285's trigger model') for the race card's own note, so the two surfaces spell one sentence rather than inventing a second one for the same fact. They are not one implementation, though: the banner's copy is composed in JavaScript from data attributes once the reader's clock says the window is open (wireElectionDay), while the race card's copy is written once, server-side, by rendering/documents.py's _certification_date_full and revealed by toggling `hidden` (wireRaceResultsCounting) -- no client-side text composition at all. The derivation is what holds the wording itself to one sentence; a reviewer moving one copy without the other is what this entry is for.

filter-scope-fallback-label.note: The payload publishes every scope label from the same generator the template renders, so the client reads the label rather than composing it. The literal that remains is a fallback for a select value the payload does not know, which the rendered markup cannot produce.

comparison-certified-result-column-label.note: Two different features coincidentally choosing the same two words, not one implementation: #287's endorsements dialog names its certified strip 'Certified result' server-side, and #288's Comparisons column picker names its addable column the same way, entirely client-side (the server never renders this column -- it is not one of compare.html.j2's three default columns, so no server occurrence of the phrase exists for the comparison page itself). Kept consistent on purpose, the same reasoning view-toggle-labels records for 'Full'/'Compact'.

$comment: Mirrors #240 was written against that no longer exist, recorded so the next reader
does not go looking for them. Each is the 'prefer deleting a mirror' rule applied.
deleted.renderer.py _race_detail_accessible_summ: Not deleted, relocated: #242 split renderer.py, and this is rendering/context.py race_detail_accessible_summary. Its client half survives and is fixtured.
deleted.audited accessible summary: #236 moved the audited value into the payload as audited_accessible_summary, so nothing recomputes it to restore the default view.
deleted.audited candidate order: #236 publishes the order the renderer rendered; the client no longer re-sorts.
deleted.sources tree strings: #248 gave the tree to lit reading payload strings, so its endorsement counts and category tags have no second implementation.
deleted.election-day phrasing: rendering/shell.py publishes the full and short dates as data attributes; election-day.mjs chooses copy but formats no date.
deleted.source participation label: rendering/payload.py source_participation_label feeds the template and the payload from one definition, replacing a Jinja macro.
deleted.race-detail-lens-count: Deleted with the counts it mirrored. A candidate heading no longer states how many sources endorsed them, because those sources are the rows listed directly below it — so neither side spells 'of N endorsing sources' or its co-endorsement parenthetical.
deleted.share-accessible-label: #314 replaced the meter's spoken label with meter-accessible-label: the full standings (docs/METER_V2.md, The discovery model's accessibility model), not a restatement of the resting percentage. screen_share_accessible_label and shareAccessibleLabel are both deleted; nothing calls either.
deleted.race-detail-mini-meter: The race page's per-candidate mini-meter (v1's own per-candidate meter, beside a tied leader's 'Tied for lead' kicker) retired with meter v2 (docs/METER_V2.md, Chrome geometry; Decision log #20) — the candidate-context treatment on the shared headline bar replaces its job in #315. race-detail.mjs's detailMeterClasses/detailMeterTemplate and race.html.j2's matching block are deleted; the kicker text alone survives.
